titulo: The complete genitive: Genitive singular and plural

aula.objetivo: Form the genitive singular and plural and use it for absence, possession, quantity, origin and the most frequent prepositions.

blocos.texto: (or: the case of origin — and the first half of the most famous case in Russian)

blocos.explicacao: Picture a scene you will probably live. You are in Russia, in a shop, and you want to say that you have no money. You think: "money in Russian is де́ньги, so I will say у меня́ нет де́ньги." The person looks at you and corrects: — У меня́ нет де́нег. You stare. It is the same word, де́ньги, but now it is де́нег, with no -и at the end. You wonder: "Haven't I already changed this word once? Why did it change again? How many forms does it have?" This happens to every learner of Russian the first time they meet the genitive, and it is where many give up. Let me be honest: this is the most complex case in Russian. But in this lesson I will do two things. STEP 1: I will explain the genitive so clearly that it looks simple. STEP 2: I will split the genitive over two lessons so you do not quit halfway. This is lesson 27: the genitive as "of" and as negation. Only that: no plural, no numbers, no prepositions; those wait for lesson 28. And before we begin, some reassurance: you are finishing the tedious part of Russian. The essential grammar ends here. What comes next is not harder, it is richer. First, what does "genitive" mean? A little etymology helps. The word comes from Latin genitivus, a Latin version of a Greek term meaning the case of the "kind" or "family" something belongs to; it is related to genus, to gignere ("to beget") and to the words gene and genetics. So the genitive is the case of origin and belonging. When you say "Ivan's book", you are saying that the book belongs to Ivan, comes from Ivan, is tied to Ivan. Unlike many languages, English has two ways to do this: "of" (the book of the teacher, the centre of the city, the colour of the sea) and the ending 's (Ivan's book, my mother's house). Look: in all these phrases the "of" or the 's shows possession, belonging or origin. That is what the genitive does in Russian. It is the case of "of" and of 's. And genetics is a nice memory hook: the genitive is the "genetic case" of the sentence, the case that marks whom a thing comes from.

blocos.titulo: Genitive singular: the "of" and the endings
blocos.explicacao: A bridge with English. Before any table, let us build the bridge. English expresses the genitive in two ways. Way 1, with "of": the book of Ivan. The house of my mother. Way 2, with 's: Ivan's book. My mother's house. In Russian, this is where the two meet: there is no separate word "of" and no 's. What exists is a change in the ending of the noun. Кни́га Ива́на is literally "book Ivan-of" (Ivan with the genitive ending). That is why the case is called the genitive: it marks origin, possession, belonging, with no word "of", only with an ending. The endings of the genitive singular. Now the endings. The method is the same as always: STEP 1: find the nominative form (the dictionary form). STEP 2: add the genitive ending, which depends on the gender and on the ending of the word. STEP 3: done, the noun is in the genitive. Notice: masculine and neuter take -А/-Я. Feminine takes -Ы/-И (or -ИИ after -ия). Neuter in -мя takes -ЕНИ. That is all. Let us see each case in detail.

tabelas.titulo: The endings of the genitive singular

linhas.GENITIVE SINGULAR: -Ы (or -И after г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, щ)

blocos.explicacao: The MASCULINE in the genitive. Masculine in a consonant → -А. Notice: the -А is added at the end of the word. Masculine in -й → -Я. Notice: the -й disappears and -Я comes in. Masculine in -ь → -Я. Notice: the -ь disappears and -Я comes in. Watch the stress: слова́рь → словаря́ (stress on the ending), but учи́тель → учи́теля (stress on the stem). There is no fixed rule. You have to listen and memorise.

The genitive answers «кого? чего?» (of whom? of what?). It is the most used case in Russian. Singular (seen already): -а → -ы; -я → -и; consonant → -а; masculine -й and -ь → -я; -о → -а; -е → -я; feminine -ь → -и. After г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, щ write -и. Plural: masculine: consonant → -ов (стол → столов); -й → -ев (музей → музеев); -ь, ж, ч, ш, щ → -ей (словарь → словарей, врач → врачей). Feminine and neuter: the ending disappears (zero): книга → книг, окно → окон. But -я → -ь (неделя → недель) and -ие → -ий. Sometimes a fleeting vowel appears: сестра → сестёр, девушка → девушек. Irregular: друзья → друзей, дети → детей, люди → людей, семья → семей.
blocos.comparacao: English uses «of» for almost everything («the brother's book», «without books»). In Russian the word changes its ending instead of getting an «of».

blocos.enunciado: Say: «У меня нет книг. У нас нет столов. У него нет друзей.»
Write the genitive singular of 6 words you already know.
